A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian Loss Smoothing research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original certified-training experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, CNN5 results on MNIST, and PGPE ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original PGPE experiments and reports additional randomized gradient smoothing experiments on CNN5, including results in Table 2 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.4 adds Randomized Gradient Smoothing (RGS), which averages gradients at Gaussian-perturbed weights and schedules the smoothing width. This introduces a substantially different training procedure alongside the retained PGPE loss-difference estimator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate certified classification on MNIST at perturbation radii 0.1 and 0.3 and CIFAR-10 at 2/255 and 8/255. Additional CNN5 and CNN7 comparisons change model configurations within this existing dataset and threat-model coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes SABR and STAPS from the CNN3 MNIST 0.1 comparison, although both remain in CNN5 comparisons. v2's CNN5 comparisons add MTL-IBP and an IBP-CNN7 reference, substantially revising the comparator set.

E3.justification: Standard training changes its reported initialization from Kaiming uniform to IBP initialization and its starting learning rate from 5e-5 to 5e-4. v2 also introduces two-sample RGS protocols with shorter training schedules and CNN7 comparison settings. These reported revisions do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The population-size, smoothing-width, training-dynamics, and loss-landscape analyses are retained. The PGPE ablations mainly move from v1 Section 4.2 and Appendix B.6 to v2 Appendix C. Additional CNN5 benchmark scores do not introduce a distinct ablation design.

E5.justification: Both versions report confidence intervals for the same 128-sample loss-smoothing plot, numbered Figure 6 in v1 and Figure 5 in v2. Neither adds benchmark seed counts, repeated-run statistics, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes CNN3 DeepPoly-GRAD certified accuracy on MNIST 0.3 from 47.28% to 66.69%, alongside reported protocol revisions. v1's CNN5 PGPE comparison is replaced by RGS results, including 97.56% certified accuracy on MNIST 0.1 and 54.83% on CIFAR-10 2/255. Larger-radius failures and revised timing results are also reported. These are changed or newly reported results, not direct same-setting version-to-version gains.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 adds mathematical analysis of smoothing quantized functions and aligning minima. Appendix B.3 analyzes RGS failure conditions and supplies a two-dimensional counterexample. Appendix B.1 also extends the differentiability derivation beyond v1 Appendix A.

C1.justification: The central claim about overcoming the certified-training paradox remains. v2 adds RGS as a fourth main contribution, claims up to 40-fold speedup, and shifts the abstract and conclusion's architecture-matched state-of-the-art performance claim toward this cheaper approximation.

C2.justification: v2 explains that RGS need not recover Gaussian-smoothed-loss gradients and can fail on discontinuous landscapes. Appendix D attributes poorer large-radius certification to insufficient regularization. Appendix A also replaces generic broader-impact language with specific concerns about attacks outside the certification assumptions and computational energy costs.

D1.justification: v2 adds RGS batch sizes, training schedules, learning-rate and smoothing-width decay information. It revises hardware reporting to L4 GPUs and identifies CNN5 PGPE costs as estimates from one epoch. Most existing architecture, preprocessing, and PGPE training documentation remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Duchi et al. (2012) to position RGS and expands the role of the already-cited Starnes et al. (2023). He et al. (2015) and Müller et al. (2021) disappear from the references. The main positioning against prior certified-training and PGPE work remains.

P1.justification: The paper substantially reorganizes its narrative: ablations move into Appendix C, broader impact moves into Appendix A, and the proof and training appendices are restructured. The abstract, introduction, scalability discussion, and conclusion are rewritten around two smoothing approaches.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a predominantly single-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. The IBP and DeepPoly illustrations become one multipanel figure, while CNN5 comparison and computational-cost tables are redesigned and expanded.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves prohibitive PGPE cost as a central unresolved limitation. v2 substantially addresses it through an implemented RGS alternative, CNN5 comparisons on both datasets, reproducibility details, and explicit theoretical and empirical failure conditions. This materially improves practical usefulness and the evidence supporting scalability. Some earlier PGPE comparisons are removed, and the maximum speedup relies on one-epoch PGPE cost estimates; these qualifications limit, but do not outweigh, the gains.
